name: The five hindrances (nīvaraṇa)
description: The first field of dhamma-contemplation in MN 10:36. In MN 10:36 the monk knows it as present or absent in himself, knows how the unarisen arises, how the arisen is abandoned and how the abandoned will not arise again; the sutta does not state the conditions for these here.

name: Covetousness and displeasure (abhijjhādomanassa)
description: What the monk puts away with regard to the world in each of the four contemplations (MN 10:3); the refrain describes clinging to nothing in the world (mn10:5).

name: The fetter (saṁyojana) arising dependent on a sense base and its object
description: In MN 10:40 the monk knows the eye and forms and the fetter that arises dependent on both, how the unarisen fetter arises, how the arisen is abandoned and how the abandoned will not arise again; likewise for the other five pairs. The sutta does not itself state the conditions.
